A.trend: Only series is an IEA scenario read from memory and labelled estimate; there is no measured series.
A.comparison: Explicitly declines to compare; no ratio or delta is given.
A.chart: Single chart of memory values labelled estimate.
A.drilldown: Layers named generically; none of the 5 follow-up calls returned data.
A.export: Estimate CSV only; provenance JSON lists no calls.
A.refs: IPCC and IEA URLs are real, but there are no DOIs and only one quote.
A.accuracy: No contradiction of the record. The scenario points are approximate and honestly labelled (the 2030 value looks low versus NZE).
A.limits: Honest and specific about what was not measured, but cannot place window or lane limits next to numbers.
A.verdict: Direct answer with decision and confidence, but it is not grounded and ignores the research-vs-patent framing.
A.facets: No grounded facets: volumes, stance, trend, geography and patents are all unanswered.

B.trend: Capacity series is from memory and labelled estimate.
B.comparison: Numeric comparison table (pipeline and scenarios vs baseline) built entirely from memory.
B.drilldown: Breakdown layers come from memory; 4 of 7 follow-up calls executed with data, but nothing was folded back into the report.
B.refs: One DOI (IPCC AR6) resolves; the others are generic URLs with no quotes.
B.accuracy: Memory figures are broadly plausible (about 50 Mt operating, 45Q at $85/t); no contradiction of the record.
B.limits: States knowledge cutoff, chart window gap and absence of lanes, but the limits are not tied to measured numbers.
B.verdict: Opinionated and useful decision with a low-medium confidence and its reason, but it rests on unverified numbers.

C.trend: Full 24-month news series traced; peak 638 in Oct-2024, CAGR -15.7% and 0.87x stated; research CAGR 14.3% stated; censoring noted in limits. Critical share is described but not charted as a decomposition.
C.comparison: Early vs late thirds across three series, all traced, with the warning not to mix windows. It does not contrast patents against research.
C.chart: One fully traced chart tied to a claim. The research trend and critical share are not charted.
C.drilldown: Traced stance, country and institution layers; 3 of 6 follow-up calls returned data.
C.export: Two traced CSVs plus provenance JSON. The news CSV is a 7-of-24-month excerpt, which is disclosed in prose but flagged coverage=full in the CSV.
C.repro: 69 of 69 numbers traced; prism-calls block lists c1 and c2 with args.
C.refs: All 6 DOIs resolve; quotes match key_numbers sentences verbatim; tiers stated.
C.accuracy: Stated as the reference has it. Contested share of 12.5% recomputes correctly. Catches the 1,515 vs 10,735 news mismatch, the 32 blank patent assignees and the undefined 'critical' label.
C.limits: Window ends with gap to today, censoring, mention match mode, the health literature index thinness, title-only patents and counts-as-documents are each placed near their numbers.
C.verdict: Bounded answer with decision, confidence and reason, and what would change it; it barely uses the patent lane.
C.facets: Volumes, stance, trends, geography and institutions are grounded; the patent-vs-research story the question highlights is not developed.

D.trend: Research series given only as endpoints. The '2.2x increase' is misattributed: 2.2 is late_vs_early thirds, while the endpoints give 2.91x. The news peak is not named.
D.comparison: News early vs late third, with the 476 delta correct and the baseline defined; there is only one comparison and no patent contrast.
D.chart: One two-point research chart whose caption repeats the 2.2x misreading; the news series is not charted.
D.drilldown: Ceiling is 1; none of the follow-up calls returned data.
D.export: Full 24-month traced CSV with a provenance block, referenced from the prose; only one table.
D.repro: Calls c1 and c2 are declared without feature or args.
D.refs: All 7 DOIs resolve; quote is verbatim; tiers stated.
D.accuracy: Misreads late_vs_early (2.2) as the endpoint growth factor; otherwise faithful.
D.limits: Specific limits: censoring, 144-day gap (correct), mention matching, overlapping labels, lane distinctions.
D.verdict: Bounded, but the decision is thin and does not engage the contrary or patent evidence.
D.facets: Skips available geography and institution data; patents appear only as a count.

C: news_monthly.csv is a 7-of-24-month excerpt but is labelled coverage=full
Institution list skips China University of Petroleum, East China (rank 3 by lift)
D: States research rose '2.2x' from 8,225 to 23,935; 2.2 is the tool's late_vs_early ratio, and the endpoint ratio is 2.91x
prism-calls entries c1 and c2 have no feature or args

raw.verdict: C was the only deliverable that grounded volumes, stance mix, both trend windows and three-lens geography in traced numbers. It also caught the 1,515 vs 10,735 news-count anomaly and placed its limits next to the numbers. D was clean and well referenced, but it misread the tool's 2.2x thirds ratio as endpoint growth and left the available geography data unused. A and B were honest memory briefs with estimate labels that a decision-maker could not verify. None of the four seriously developed the patents-vs-research contrast the question flagged.
